Subject: Onboarding: VAT / PO questions for Northern Ireland operations

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the onboarding link — we are ready to kick off. A couple of things came up on our side specific to our Northern Ireland entity (SveaNordics Ltd - NI branch):

- Which VAT proof do you need for NI-registered suppliers? We have a VAT registration letter and recent VAT returns.
- Do you route POs to a UK billing entity or to your EU entity for NI suppliers? (we sell both goods and services into EU customers)
- Any special invoice fields required to avoid VAT being incorrectly charged or withheld?

I can attach our VAT certificate and a sample invoice if that helps.

Wanted to get alignment before we hand documents to our finance team.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Onboarding: VAT / PO questions for Northern Ireland operations

Tom — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers and next steps below; attaching our NI playbook and PO-routing template to make it concrete.

High level:
- Required docs: VAT registration certificate (official letter or PDF from HMRC), a recent VAT return (latest quarter), and a company registration extract showing the NI business address. We also accept a bank statement with the company name/address if HMRC docs are delayed.
- PO routing: For Northern Ireland suppliers that trade primarily into the EU (goods moved to EU customers), procurement will route POs to Redwood's EU billing entity so VAT treatment aligns with the destination EU rules. For NI services or UK-only sales, POs go to our UK billing entity.
- Invoice fields: please include supplier VAT number, invoice currency, and line-level country of supply if goods move across borders; add Purchase Order number exactly as in the PO.

Next steps:
1) If you can, upload the VAT certificate + VAT return to the secure intake link (see playbook).
2) We will confirm billing entity selection and send a PO example with the exact invoice header we need.
3) Procurement/legal may request an additional attest form for NI/EU movement — Laura will confirm below.

I'll kick off the internal routing now so you have the PO template by EOD.

Best,
Hannah
Senior Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments: NI_VAT_Onboarding_Playbook.pdf (attached), PO_Routing_Mapping_Template.xlsx (attached)

From: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:17:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Onboarding: VAT / PO questions for Northern Ireland operations

Looping in for tax/legal confirmation. Quick notes for procurement playbook:

- When goods originate in NI but are sold into EU customers, we treat the supplier as an EU-supplied-good counterparty for PO mapping only — operationally we map invoices to the EU billing entity to avoid incorrect UK VAT charges. This is consistent with our existing NI-to-EU supplier cases but requires a VAT certificate and a statement of typical supply flows (we use a short attestation template).
- For services: default to reverse charge where applicable; supplier must supply a valid VAT number and indicate business-to-business status on invoice.
- We should request a signed "trade flow attestation" from the supplier describing whether their NI entity regularly sells goods into the EU — this can be a one-page PDF.

Ben — can you add the attestation to the PO_Routing_Mapping_Template and mark a flag for EU-mapped suppliers so AP has routing metadata?

Laura
Head of Tax Compliance | Redwood Inference

Tom — appreciate the quick turnaround and docs. Confirming the operational path so your finance team can proceed: 

- Upload: please use the secure intake link in the playbook. Once we validate the VAT cert + attestation we will tag your supplier record with "EU-mapped: true" in the PO template.
- Remit-to field: we prefer the supplier to keep the remit-to as your legal NI entity for payment. PO-level routing is sufficient for tax mapping; AP will not reject invoices that list your NI legal name.
- VAT treatment on invoice: leave the VAT rate/amount blank and include the wording "B2B reverse charge may apply; VAT to be accounted by recipient" and the supplier VAT number on the invoice. AP will then process according to the PO routing.

We will send you a sample PO (with the EU-billing header and the internal routing tag) by close of business today. After we validate documents, we can move to active supplier status and issue the first PO.

If legal needs anything further we'll reach out, but this should be sufficient for your team to upload.

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Accounts Payable Manager | Redwood Inference
